newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi explosion kills one, wounds four.
newsitem.headline: Karachi explosion kills one, wounds four.

text.p: An explosion rocked Pakistan's troubled port city of Karachi on Monday, killing one man and wounding four people, including three children, police said.
They said the blast had occurred on the first floor of an unfinished house in the central Liaquatabad area, a stronghold of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
"A 22-year-old man was killed, while three children and a woman were wounded in the blast," a police officer said.
The explosion damaged the single-storey building, which was still under construction.
Bomb Disposal Squad chief Moin Khan said the blast was powerful and the device that caused it could have been home-made.
"Most probably, the device exploded in the victim's hands while he was handling it. But our investigations are not yet complete," he told Reuters.
Witnesses said the roof of the room where the device blew-up had caved in and the walls were badly damaged.
Four passers-by, including three children and a woman, were wounded by the explosion.
More than 155 people have been killed in political violence in Karachi during the past four months, compared to 500 in 1996 and 2,000 in 1995.
